newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Duisenberg confirmed as EMI chief from July 97.
newsitem.headline: Duisenberg confirmed as EMI chief from July 97.

text.p: The European Union summit on Friday formally adopted Dutch central bank chief Wim Duisenberg as president of the European Monetary Institute (EMI) from July 1, 1997, an EU spokesman said.
The EU leaders also re-appointed current EMI president Alexandre Lamfalussy to continue in the post for the first six months of next year.
Both moves were initially announced last summer, but needed summit approval.
The EMI is the forerunner of the European Central Bank which will govern the 15-member bloc's monetary policy from January 1, 1999 as part of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).

Duisenberg is currently Europe's longest-serving central bank chief, and the Dutch economy, with its strong guilder, low inflation and unemployment and tight fiscal policy, is widely regarded as a model for Europe's economic future.
